scope: Revision 002 of the offline device-2 HID report-descriptor inspection rules. Revision 001 remains reports/sprint-010/trackpad-descriptor-inspection-plan.json and is not edited. The only change is metadata acceptance: advertised input is any nonzero uint16. Descriptor length stays 1..512. The transport and on-wire ceiling stay 2038. No descriptor bytes are invented here. No mode write, GET, SET, build, SSH, or hardware action is specified or performed.
delta_from_revision_001: Replace the acceptance predicate 'input length in 1..2038' and the confirmation clause that applied an input-report cap only when max_input was inside 1..2038. Those clauses would refuse the real advertised input 2048 before the descriptor walk. Advertised max_input is now any nonzero uint16 and is not parser capacity. An on-wire report still may not exceed 2038. Feature report 2 still has to be exactly 2 bytes inside the same application-collection and local-usage rules. Nothing else in the gate moves.

names.capture_T1: The enumeration capture: two read queries, then the 556-byte PDM1TrackpadEnumerationV1 record. Qualification criteria T1 through T7 in reports/sprint-010/trackpad-enum-qualification-criteria-002.json govern that capture. Criteria id T3 there is retrieval of the raw record, not a mode write.
names.mode_gate: The first device-2 feature write in reports/sprint-010/native-trackpad-spi-dev2-plan.json phase T3, as restated by native-trackpad-spi-dev2-plan-addendum-001.json. This plan defines the descriptor evidence that gate requires. It does not open the write.

actor: Root is the sole test actor. When a saved attempt 002 record is provided, the independent decode of its descriptor bytes follows this revision. This receipt does not ask for that capture. Attempt 001 stays a metadata refusal with descriptor_bytes 0 and is not inspected under either revision.

input_when_a_capture_exists.accept_only: One collector receipt whose verdict is ENUMERATION_CAPTURED, exit 0, result 0, stage 5, request mask 31, metadata header byte 1 equal to 2, metadata payload in 16..2038, advertised input a nonzero uint16 (1..65535, including 2048 and 65535), descriptor_bytes in 1..512, and descriptor_payload_bytes equal to descriptor_bytes. The descriptor is record bytes [44, 44+descriptor_bytes). Bytes [44+descriptor_bytes, 556) stay zero. The advertised input is diagnostic. It does not enlarge the 2038 transport payload or the 512-byte descriptor copy.
input_when_a_capture_exists.bind: Nonce, SHA-256 of the whole 556-byte record, descriptor_bytes, and SHA-256 of the descriptor slice alone. Instance absent or byte-equal stays the collector's already recorded fact.
input_when_a_capture_exists.refuse: REFUSED, MISSING, MIG_ERROR, MALFORMED, INSTANCE_MISMATCH, advertised input 0, metadata payload outside 16..2038, descriptor_bytes 0, descriptor_bytes outside 1..512, or a slice that disagrees with descriptor_bytes. Those captures contain no descriptor to inspect. The keyboard interface-1 descriptor is not a substitute. Attempt 001 is in this refused set.

walk.grammar: Short items as tagged in sources/puredarwin-baseline/src/Kernel/Extensions/IOHIDFamily/IOHIDFamily/IOHIDDescriptorParserPrivate.h. Prefix bits: size 0..1, type 2..3, tag 4..7. Size code 0, 1, 2, 3 means 0, 1, 2, 4 data bytes, little-endian. Type 0 main, 1 global, 2 local. Main tags Input 8, Output 9, Collection 0x0A, Feature 0x0B, End Collection 0x0C. Global Report Size tag 7, Report ID tag 8, Report Count tag 9, Usage Page tag 0, Push 0x0A, Pop 0x0B. Local Usage tag 0, Usage Minimum 1, Usage Maximum 2. Collection data 1 is an application collection. No IOHID parser function is copied.
walk.bounds: One forward pass over the captured slice. A short item must fit in the slice. Prefix 0xFE, a pop with an empty stack, a push past 16, collection nesting past 16, or more than 64 collections fails the walk. Report ID data must be one byte, value 1..255. reportSize times reportCount, and each report's accumulated bit count, must not imply an on-wire report longer than 2038 bytes. That 2038 ceiling is the transport payload cap. Advertised input 2048 or 65535 does not raise it. Failure leaves no partial confirmation.
walk.lengths: Data bits for one Input, Output, or Feature item are reportSize times reportCount, and constant items count. Report ID bytes are not inside those data bits. When any Report ID item exists, the on-wire length of a report that has at least one matching main item is 1 plus (dataBits + 7) / 8. This is the same split IOHID uses when it starts a new report's bit count at 8 for the ID and later returns (bitCount + 7) / 8, ignoring an ID whose bit count never grows past 8 (HIDGetReportLength.c). Input, output, and feature counts stay separate for the same numeric ID.
walk.usages: A 1- or 2-byte local usage uses the current Usage Page. A 4-byte local usage uses its high 16 bits as the page and its low 16 bits as the usage. Local usages apply to the next main item and then clear. Each application collection records the local usage in effect at its Collection item.

required_together: At least one Report ID item exists.
At least one Feature main item is emitted while the current Report ID is 2, and those Feature items add at least one data bit.

The on-wire length of feature report 2 is 2 bytes. The pinned J293 write is the two bytes {0x02, 0x01}: report ID 0x02 and one data byte (hid-magicmouse.c feature_mt_trackpad2_usb, hid_hw_raw_request HID_FEATURE_REPORT / HID_REQ_SET_REPORT).
That Feature item sits inside an application collection whose usage page and usage were both present.
Each Feature item of report 2 has at least one local usage, or a usage minimum/maximum pair.

Every input report's on-wire length is at most the lesser of the advertised nonzero max_input and 2038. Where max_output or max_control is nonzero, output or feature on-wire length is at most the lesser of that value and 2038. A recorded 0 for output or control is an absent diagnostic cap, not a zero-byte limit. An advertised max_input above 2038 does not permit an on-wire report above 2038 and does not change the 2-byte feature-report-2 rule.
not_sufficient: An Input item with report ID 2. magicmouse's SPI input path looks at data[0] == 0x02 and registers an input report of size 6; that size is the driver's stub, not a descriptor length.
The transport comment row 'mt mode: 0x40 0x02 0x52 0x02 0x00', or the SET_REPORT mapping command 0x52 / report 0x02 / payload {0x02, 0x01}. Those name the write. They are not the device descriptor.
A lone 0x02 or 0xB1 byte without a finished Feature item under report ID 2.
Interface metadata, country, an advertised input of 2048, or the keyboard descriptor.

inventory_always_recorded: For every input, output, and feature report: ID, data bit count, on-wire byte length, and the enclosing application usage page and usage.

Whether input report 0x02, input report 0x60, and feature report 0xD9 occur, with their lengths. Input 0x02 and reset 0x60 are magicmouse's SPI report IDs. Feature 0xD9 is the 32-byte dimensions GET, which stays a separate review and is not authorized here.

The application usages named only as labels for whatever the bytes contain: Generic Desktop Pointer 0x01/0x01, Mouse 0x01/0x02, Digitizer Touch Pad 0x0D/0x05, Touch Screen 0x0D/0x04, Finger 0x0D/0x22 (IOHIDUsageTables.h). None of these numbers is required for FEATURE_02_CONFIRMED. The captured values are the usage evidence.
effect: FEATURE_02_CONFIRMED is the descriptor evidence the mode gate asks for. It is not permission to send the write, to issue GET 0xD9, to touch device 3, or to claim pointer input. FEATURE_02_NOT_CONFIRMED keeps that gate closed. Accepting advertised input 2048 only lets a complete descriptor reach this inspection. Pre-mode report behaviour remains unobserved.
